concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds on running time up to a constant factor.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of coefficients times powers of an indeterminate, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a, b, including roots of unity and the modulus.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes, each head moving at most one cell per step.

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.title: The $n\log n$ optimality conjecture

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's 1971 conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of growth for multiplying n-bit integers on a multitape Turing machine.

evidence.quote: The theorem refutes an eventual $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound for every fixed multiplication machine in this model.
Sch\"onhage and Strassen conjectured $n\log n$ as the optimal order of multiplication cost

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier
concepts.title: Established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each input of the subroutine multiplication.

symbols.name: big-O bound
symbols.meaning: Asymptotic upper bound up to a constant factor.

concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's fixed-tape O(n log n) integer multiplication algorithm, used here only as an ordinary subroutine on short records.

evidence.quote: Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of coefficient arrays in which indices add modulo the array length, i.e. polynomial multiplication modulo x^S − 1.

evidence.quote: Thus convolution modulo $x^S-1$ has no nonzero wraparound.
let $*$ denote cyclic convolution in the displayed axes

concepts.name: Radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing each input as a polynomial in 2^b, so that the product becomes a convolution of small digit coefficients followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.
Write the two inputs as polynomials in $2^b$, each with $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ nonnegative digits.

concepts.name: Normalized discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The map sending a length-q vector to its averages against the q-th roots of unity; it is a contraction and turns cyclic convolution into pointwise multiplication.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction, since each output averages inputs multiplied by complex numbers of modulus one.

concepts.name: Array streams and logical volume
concepts.gloss: Arrays are stored on tape in lexicographic order of their address fields with implicit addresses, and the logical volume V is the number of stored data bits.

evidence.quote: An address is implicit in an entry's position in this ordered stream; it is not stored beside every data bit.
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Linear-time tape operations that permute or move a single fixed-radix digit of the address, split and merge streams on a digit, and split rows cyclically into a fixed number of streams.

evidence.quote: moving one specified radix-$q$ digit to another position, preserving the order of the intervening positions;

concepts.name: Controlled shifts
concepts.gloss: A linear-time update adding to a later address field an offset computed from earlier control fields (or scaling it by a fixed unit), implemented by splitting and remerging blocks.

evidence.quote: The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: The isomorphism x ↦ ∏ x_i^{μ_i} that turns one cyclic convolution of length S = ∏ s_i into a multidimensional cyclic convolution on distinct prime axes, implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves.

evidence.quote: Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution
Each triangular update is a prefix-controlled cyclic shift.

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's identity expressing a Fourier transform of prime length s through one of nearby power-of-two length t, using Gaussian-weighted contractions.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling connects these two shapes.
it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

concepts.name: Resampling with retained permutations
concepts.gloss: Keeping the coordinate permutations P_s and P_t inside the resampling identity P_sF_s = 2^{2α²}B₀P_tF_tA instead of sorting, and letting the source permutation cancel across forward transforms, pointwise product, and opposite transform.

evidence.quote: Here the source and target permutations remain in the transform identity, while the faster tape procedures perform the required axis movements.
Finally, the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product, and the opposite-sign transform.

concepts.name: Tensor resampling interface
concepts.gloss: Applying the one-dimensional resampling maps line by line along each of d axes of a padded power-of-two box, with axis exposure done by chunk interchanges.

evidence.quote: For the tensor product, apply the one-dimensional maps to one coordinate line at a time.

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Writing a Fourier transform, including its frequency permutation, as pointwise multiplication by a chirp, a cyclic convolution with the chirp, and another chirp multiplication.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$

symbols.name: ring indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The polynomial variable whose powers act as synthetic roots of unity.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials of degree below r with y^r = −1, where multiplication by a power of y is a signed cyclic shift of coefficients.

evidence.quote: Multiplication by $y^a$, for any integer $a$, permutes the coefficients and changes some signs; consequently it is an isometry for this norm.

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: The map x_d ↦ ζy with ζ = e^{πi/r} that converts cyclic convolution along the last axis into negacyclic multiplication modulo y^r + 1.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.

concepts.name: Normalized butterfly H₀
concepts.title: Normalized butterfly $H_0$

symbols.name: normalized butterfly
symbols.meaning: The two-point linear map sending (u, v) to ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2).

concepts.gloss: The two-point map (u, v) ↦ ((u+v)/2, (u−v)/2), the basic step of radix-two Fourier transforms.

evidence.quote: In this representation, the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations.

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadics and fixed-point truncation
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators, stored exactly in fixed-point words and truncated toward zero to the p-bit grid only at the end of a layer.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics, whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.
A single truncation follows the completed contractive layer.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A radix-two Fourier transform over the ring modulo y^r + 1 whose roots of unity are powers of y, so twiddles are signed shifts; its output is stored in bit-reversed frequency order.

evidence.quote: Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list.
These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Linear bank-exchange network
concepts.gloss: A fixed finite network of linear gates on wires (roles) that exchanges two banks of values with prescribed signs while restoring every auxiliary scratch value.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.

concepts.name: Restoration of arbitrary scratch values
concepts.gloss: An eight-row schedule that subtracts the effect of unknown scratch contents, adds the intended computation, and uncomputes, so scratch wires may start with arbitrary values.

evidence.quote: This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation

concepts.name: Three-element-subset gather and scatter
concepts.gloss: Gates indexed by three-element subsets of [100]: gather and scatter produce coefficients depending on intersection size, and side wires cancel the unwanted ones so the net effect is y ← y + x.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.

concepts.name: Frames and the common-frame identity
concepts.gloss: Storing each wire's array through an invertible operator (frame) that is common at each gate, so pointwise gates commute with frames and only endpoint frames determine the net operator.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.
At a pointwise linear gate $G$, the common frame commutes with the gate:

concepts.name: Nested subspace labels
concepts.gloss: Nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space attached to gates and terminals, nested along each edge, whose orthogonal residual dimensions count the smaller operations an edge needs.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.
the \emph{orthogonal residual} is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one

concepts.name: Rank deficit of the network
concepts.gloss: The property that the total number s of smaller calls over all edges is strictly less than the wire count W times the label dimension m.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The array permutation moving the entry at address (H, D) to (H + MD, D) for a matrix M acting on two groups of address fields.

evidence.quote: For the bit procedure, that endpoint operator is an address shear:
the frame $\Phi_M$ moves the array entry at $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$

concepts.name: Rational matrix interface
concepts.gloss: The bit network with XOR gates and rational projection matrices on its vertices, whose endpoint matrices differ by the identity on every role and whose edge ranks sum to s_b < W_b·m.

evidence.quote: The bit network has $W_{\rm b}$ wires, uses only pointwise XOR gates, and sends its input vector to the permutation $\rho$ of that vector.

concepts.name: Lower triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Writing any rational matrix of rank a as E₁ΠE₂ with invertible lower triangular E₁, E₂ and a partial permutation Π with a ones, a reversed Bruhat factorization.

evidence.quote: The rank reduction used for address shears is a singular-matrix Bruhat factorization

concepts.name: Cost of a rational matrix shear
concepts.gloss: A shear (H, D) ↦ (H + AD, D) by a fixed rational matrix of rank a costs exactly a interchanges of smaller field pairs plus linear work.

evidence.quote: can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.

concepts.name: Row splitting among roles
concepts.gloss: Distributing rows of an array cyclically among the W wire roles so that each role stream has the same address shape and volume V/W.

evidence.quote: Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles, padding the row count for each prefix to a multiple of $W$.

concepts.name: Volume-normalized recurrence
concepts.gloss: The recurrence F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1} + O(1) for cost divided by volume, which yields a power saving because s/W < m.

evidence.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Fast address chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: A fixed-tape procedure that exchanges two equal-width contiguous address chunks of u bits in O(Vu^τ) time with τ < 1, via XOR combinations of data driven by the bit network.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian product.
Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.name: Binary phase frames
concepts.gloss: Frames C_U = H^{⊗m} diag(i^{wt(P_U x) mod 4}) H^{⊗m} attached to binary labels, whose edge changes factor into one two-point kernel aI + bX_v per residual basis vector.

evidence.quote: Its phase frames express a $C$ tensor product using smaller groups of selected bits, separated by binary changes of basis.

concepts.name: Binary phase interface
concepts.gloss: The complex network with binary labels: after endpoint corrections it applies the tensor power of the kernel C on every role using s_c < W_c·m smaller kernel calls.

evidence.quote: After source and sink diagonal corrections, and undoing the signed bank exchange, telescoping these phase frames gives $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, including auxiliary roles.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: XORing selected bits of one address chunk into another by eight packed cyclic shifts with guard bits, followed by deterministic repair of an explicitly bounded set of exceptional addresses.

evidence.quote: The construction first uses a constant number of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, then corrects an explicitly bounded set of addresses.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: Applying H₀ on the same bit position in up to d address chunks at once in O(Vd^{λ'}) time, λ' < 1, by recursing through the complex network and evaluating the layer exactly before one truncation.

evidence.quote: On the layouts used in the multiplication algorithm, one selects the same bit position in each of at most $d$ equal-width address chunks, and the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$.

concepts.name: Transform layout
concepts.gloss: A positional permutation of address bits placing the bits used in each transform round at a common offset in consecutive K-bit chunks, so simultaneous layers apply and the frequency order is retained.

evidence.quote: we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing
concepts.gloss: A signed Kronecker substitution that evaluates integer polynomials at B₀ = 2^{4p}, multiplies with the established multiplier, and recovers coefficients by centered residues, giving products in the ring modulo y^r + 1.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Convolution from the retained transform layout
concepts.gloss: Normalized convolution over the polynomial ring computed by two forward synthetic transforms, pointwise packed products in the stored order, and the opposite transform consuming that order.

evidence.quote: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $LB$ to both operands.

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Undoing known scales, rounding each approximate coefficient whose error is below 1/2 to the exact integer, and propagating radix-2^b carries to obtain the binary product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product.

concepts.name: Parameter choice and cost table
concepts.gloss: Fixed rational parameters (τ = 1 − 2^{-50}, ε = 2^{-75}, κ = 2^{-182}, …) under which every term of the cost per bit is at most p^{1−2κ}.

evidence.quote: A compatible choice of rational parameters makes all terms in its cost table fit Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two input integers.

symbols.name: ceiling binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The function lg n = max{⌈log₂ n⌉, 1}.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{-182} by which the logarithmic exponent drops below one.

symbols.name: big-O bound
symbols.meaning: Asymptotic upper bound up to a constant factor on worst-case running time.

concepts.gloss: One deterministic fixed-alphabet multitape Turing machine computes the exact 2n-bit product of two n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) worst-case time with κ = 2^{-182}, refuting the n log n lower-bound conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time
$\kappa=2^{-182}$, on one fixed finite-alphabet Turing machine with a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sum of distinct powers of two, recorded as a string of bits, with an n-bit integer lying below 2^n.

concepts.name: Carry propagation
concepts.gloss: The schoolbook rule for adding numbers in positional notation, where any digit sum at least the radix passes its excess as a carry into the next position.

concepts.name: Two's complement
concepts.gloss: The representation of signed integers in w bits in which a negative x is stored as 2^w + x, so the top bit acts as the sign.

concepts.name: Exclusive or
concepts.gloss: The bit operation returning 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, equal to addition modulo 2 and its own inverse.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication
concepts.gloss: Multiplying two n-digit numbers by summing shifted partial products, which costs O(n^2) digit operations.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling
concepts.gloss: The largest integer at most x and the smallest integer at least x, respectively.

concepts.name: Rounding to the nearest integer
concepts.gloss: Replacing a real number by an integer close to it, so that a value known to within less than 1/2 of an integer determines that integer exactly.

concepts.name: Fixed-point numbers
concepts.gloss: Storing a real number as an integer times a fixed power of two, so a fixed number of bits sits after the binary point.

concepts.name: Binary logarithm
concepts.gloss: The exponent to which 2 must be raised to give x, written lg x, with other bases differing only by a constant factor inside big-O.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where two numbers are identified when their difference is divisible by a fixed modulus m.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor
concepts.gloss: The largest integer dividing both of two integers, with the integers called coprime when it equals 1.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: Integers greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and themselves, from which every positive integer is uniquely a product.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s_1, …, s_d, the map sending an integer modulo their product to its tuple of residues is a bijection.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: Proving a statement for all natural numbers by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

concepts.name: Recurrence relations for running time
concepts.gloss: Inequalities bounding an algorithm's cost on size n by its cost on smaller sizes plus extra work, solved by unrolling or the master method.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.gloss: A sum of terms with a constant ratio r, which for |r| < 1 is bounded by the first term divided by 1 − r.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: Bijections of a finite set to itself, used to reorder the entries of a sequence and composable and invertible.

concepts.name: Binomial coefficients
concepts.gloss: The number C(n, k) of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order
concepts.gloss: Ordering tuples by their first coordinate, breaking ties by the second, and so on.

concepts.name: Vectors and matrices
concepts.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers representing linear maps between coordinate spaces, multiplied by composing those maps.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
concepts.gloss: Sets closed under addition and scalar multiplication, with dimension the size of any basis, and linear maps the functions respecting both operations.

concepts.name: Matrix rank
concepts.gloss: The dimension of the column space of a matrix, equal to the maximum number of linearly independent rows or columns.

concepts.name: Invertible matrices
concepts.gloss: Square matrices with a two-sided inverse, equivalently with nonzero determinant or full rank.

concepts.name: Triangular and diagonal matrices
concepts.gloss: Square matrices whose entries above (lower triangular) or off (diagonal) the main diagonal are zero.

concepts.name: Permutation matrices
concepts.gloss: 0–1 matrices with exactly one 1 in each row and column, which reorder the coordinates of a vector.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.gloss: Reducing a matrix by elementary row and column operations to compute its rank, inverse or a triangular factorization.

concepts.name: Rational numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers p/q with integers p and q ≠ 0, forming a field over which matrices can be manipulated exactly.

concepts.name: Maximum norm
concepts.gloss: The largest absolute value of the entries of a vector, used to bound sizes and errors coordinatewise.

concepts.name: Triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: The bound saying the size of a sum is at most the sum of the sizes, used to add up error contributions.

concepts.name: Exponential function and Euler's formula
concepts.gloss: The exponential e^x, extended to complex arguments by e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, giving points on the unit circle.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science background: asymptotic analysis of algorithms and solving simple cost recurrences, basic Turing machines and multitape simulation, binary representation of integers and machine arithmetic (carries, two's complement, XOR, fixed-point rounding), and the discrete mathematics taught to everyone (induction, modular arithmetic, gcd, primes, the Chinese remainder theorem, permutations, binomial coefficients, lexicographic order). From the required mathematics they have a first course in linear algebra (vectors, matrices, rank, invertibility, triangular and diagonal matrices, linear maps over Q and C) and basic complex numbers and polynomials. They have not studied tensor products of operators, bilinear forms, Hadamard or Bruhat-type factorizations, FFT variants beyond a textbook mention, or research-level integer multiplication algorithms.
